## Description
The wallet contract (`contracts/wallet`) is the core execution agent for organizations, calling other modules and transfers. To prevent potential nested execution loops or scenarios where an external contract triggers another execution in the same wallet instance before the first call finishes, we need to introduce a transient state execution lock.

## Context & Requirements
- Soroban contracts do not support traditional reentrancy in the same thread easily, but multi-contract call graphs can create complicated execution patterns.
- An explicit state flag must be stored in the contract storage (e.g., `StorageType::Instance`) when an execution starts, and cleared when it ends.
- The lock should check if an execution is already in progress and revert with a deterministic error code `EXECUTION_LOCKED` if so.
- Must handle cleanups correctly even if internal steps exit gracefully or return early.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement an `ExecutionLock` guard or state checker using Soroban's instance storage.
- [ ] Add the execution lock check to all primary transaction execution methods in `contracts/wallet/src/lib.rs`.
- [ ] Revert with a dedicated error code `EXECUTION_LOCKED` defined in `shared` or `interfaces`.
- [ ] All standard unit tests must pass, and new tests must verify that nested execution attempts fail.

## Implementation Guidance
- Look at `contracts/wallet/src/lib.rs` (or equivalent file structure under `contracts/wallet`).
